title: Your strengths and your gaps
header_line: My analysis of one book on authority and personal brand. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What is the one strength you would give away and the weakness you would fix?

I asked each person: what is your strength as a leader, and your lack of strength? One student said empathy is a strength and the frequency of communication is a weakness. Another said adaptability and situational awareness.

I said that I asked this because we need to analyze: am I a back-end person who keeps the data under control, or a front-end person who can sit with someone and make an emotional and rational connection?

I said I can talk about my weaknesses more easily than my strengths. I said I can switch from the empathetic, servant leader to just get this done and become insensitive, and that I have a tendency to switch off while someone talks. Every day I remind myself to be a better listener.

I said that I focus on strategy and talk little about operations, so I put people in place for the day-to-day who remind me of the schedule and milestones. I said I struggle with administrative tasks.
Name your strength and your weakness, and who covers the gap.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write your strength as a leader.
Write whether you are back end or front end.
Write the one habit that would help your weakness.

check.q: What did I ask each person?
choices: Their strength and their lack of strength

check.q: What did I say I do about day-to-day operations?
choices: Puts people in place for them

check.q: What did I say I remind myself to be?

recap: Know your strength and your gap. Put someone in the gap.
